The historical referent is the establishment of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia by UN Security Council Resolution 827 (25 May 1993) under Chapter VII authority, with subject-matter jurisdiction defined by Articles 2 (grave breaches of the 1949 Geneva Conventions), 3 (violations of the laws or customs of war), 4 (genocide), and 5 (crimes against humanity) of the ICTY Statute. The Tribunal operated from The Hague between 1993 and 2017 and indicted 161 persons across all parties to the conflict. Audit-only framing applies: this annotation registers a documentary observation in the endgame Cost Ledger; it does not flip rupture wiring, does not unlock atrocity-tactic paths, and does not attribute culpability to any specific individual or unit. Counterfactual reckoning surface. UN Security Council Resolution 824 (6 May 1993) and Resolution 836 (4 June 1993) designated Sarajevo, Tuzla, Žepa, Goražde, Bihać and Srebrenica as Safe Areas under UNPROFOR mandate. The historical record finds the Safe Area regime structurally failed: ICTY Trial Chamber, Prosecutor v. Krstić (IT-98-33-T, 2 August 2001, paras. 36-46) documents the July 1995 collapse of the Srebrenica enclave and the genocide that followed, and Prosecutor v. Mladić (IT-09-92-T, 22 November 2017, paras. 2493-2581) finds command responsibility for that collapse. This annotation records a sustained run-state in which the Safe Area mandate is enforced past t145 — the counterfactual that the international protection framework on paper had been honoured in practice. The annotation describes the documented institutional regime; it does not attribute culpability for any specific historical event.

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo authorizes clearance operations against APWB. Mostar reads the decision as Sarajevo holding the line against an internal Bosniak fracture; alliance signaling on the Federation track is preserved.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH presses suppression of the Abdic split

pending_event_notifications.body: The Presidency holds the line of non-recognition and clears 5th Corps for clearance operations against the Velika Kladusa axis. Pale reads the decision as Sarajevo committing to a Bihac-pocket military solution; VRS coordinates support for APWB through RSK channels.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo authorizes 5th Corps clearance of APWB

pending_event_notifications.body: The Herceg-Bosna presidency calls for cohesion across the divided pockets. Sarajevo reads a leadership managing exposure more than promising gains.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar asks its community to hold

pending_event_notifications.body: The Herceg-Bosna presidency appeals for endurance. Pale sees the HVO preparing for a long hold.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar asks its community to hold

pending_event_notifications.body: The RBiH presidency turns its address outward, naming the siege for an international audience. Mostar sees a diplomatic-pressure move with a patron-goodwill cost attached.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo appeals to the world

pending_event_notifications.body: The RBiH presidency presses the international community over the siege. Pale sees Sarajevo trading patron patience for outside attention.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo appeals to the world

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency calls for consolidation rather than advance. Mostar reads a leadership managing strain more than promising gains.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale asks its people to hold

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency appeals for endurance and consolidation. Sarajevo sees Pale preparing its public for a long hold.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale asks its people to hold

pending_event_notifications.body: Pale looks for a way back toward Belgrade after the embargo. Mostar sees reduced immediate supply shock for RS if talks hold, at the cost of visible internal cohesion.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS moves to soften Belgrade break

pending_event_notifications.body: RS opens back-channel accommodation with Milosevic and signals room to revisit the Contact Group map. Sarajevo sees possible relief for RS supply pressure, but also internal strains inside Pale.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale seeks accommodation with Belgrade

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo authorizes the Bihac-pocket offensive. Mostar reads the decision as Sarajevo holding the line against the Abdic split and signals continued Federation military coordination.
pending_event_notifications.headline: 5th Corps cleared for autumn-1994 offensive

pending_event_notifications.body: The Presidency clears Dudakovic to press Grabez and overrun Velika Kladusa. Pale reads the decision as Sarajevo committing to a Bihac-axis military solution; VRS coordinates the counter-attack with RSK and APWB.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo authorizes 5th Corps Bihac offensive

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo commits to honoring the Carter pause while resupplying and rebuilding. Mostar sees the Federation side preserving diplomatic credibility during the temporary quiet.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH respects winter ceasefire

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH signals compliance with the winter cessation of hostilities and uses the pause to rebuild. Pale sees lower immediate offensive pressure and improved international standing for Sarajevo.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo honors Carter ceasefire

pending_event_notifications.body: RS Crisis Staff issues public denial of detention-camp operations and refuses outside investigator access at the Prijedor-area sites. Mostar registers Belgrade patron pressure rising as international attention fixes on Omarska and Trnopolje.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Crisis Staff denies camp existence (ICTY Karadzic IT-95-5/18-T §§3473-3475)

pending_event_notifications.body: RS Crisis Staff issues public denial of detention-camp operations and refuses outside investigator access at the Prijedor-area sites. Sarajevo registers Belgrade patron pressure rising as international attention fixes on Omarska and Trnopolje.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Crisis Staff denies camp existence (ICTY Karadzic IT-95-5/18-T §§3473-3475)

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo signals acceptance of the proposed territorial framework under international pressure. Mostar sees Federation diplomacy aligned for now, with the military and political burden shifting toward RS refusal.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH accepts the Contact Group plan

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the proposed 51/49 Contact Group framework. Pale faces a stronger international-credibility case for Sarajevo and sharper scrutiny if RS remains outside the plan.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Contact Group map

pending_event_notifications.body: The Herceg-Bosna presidency honours one of the HVO's regular formations. Sarajevo reads a morale gesture and the politics of favour across the divided geography.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar decorates a regular HVO formation

pending_event_notifications.body: The Herceg-Bosna presidency awards a citation to a regular HVO formation. Pale sees a morale signal and the internal balance it shifts.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar decorates a regular HVO formation

pending_event_notifications.body: The RBiH presidency recognises its regular formations collectively rather than singling one out. Mostar reads a cohesion-minded, lower-key gesture.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo issues a broad army citation

pending_event_notifications.body: The RBiH presidency honours the regular army as a whole. Pale sees a unifying but modest morale move.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo issues a broad army citation

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency honours one of the VRS's regular formations. Mostar reads a morale gesture and the politics of favour within the officer corps.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale decorates a regular VRS formation

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency awards a citation to a regular VRS formation. Sarajevo sees a morale signal and the internal jockeying it implies.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale decorates a regular VRS formation

pending_event_notifications.body: RS command records the Drina field reports and opens a chain-of-command review. Mostar sees an accountability order whose practical force remains to be demonstrated.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS opens a Drina command review

pending_event_notifications.body: RS command enters field reports from the Drina Valley into an official accountability process and requires written civilian-protection orders. Sarajevo will judge the order by conduct around Zvornik, Višegrad, and Foča.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS opens a Drina command review

pending_event_notifications.body: Herceg-Bosna sends reinforcements into the Gornji Vakuf clashes. Sarajevo staff see a significant escalation in the HVO-ARBiH confrontation and a sharper break in local cooperation.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO reinforces Gornji Vakuf fight

pending_event_notifications.body: Herceg-Bosna answers the Gornji Vakuf clashes with force. Pale analysts see the Vance-Owen provincial map becoming a boundary dispute for deeper Croat-Bosniak fighting.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO and ARBiH fighting intensifies

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo accepts the two-month ceasefire framework. Mostar sees Federation momentum capped, but US support and negotiating leverage remain intact.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH accepts ceasefire demand

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH agrees to halt the northwestern offensive and preserve the path to Dayton talks. Pale sees front pressure pause, while Sarajevo improves patron confidence and international standing.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Holbrooke ceasefire

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar declines to discipline HVO commanders in Prozor, Novi Travnik, and Vitez. Sarajevo reads the silence as confirmation that the joint anti-VRS front is degrading through structural dispute rather than central decision.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HZ HB accepts Graz baseline; local frictions harden

pending_event_notifications.body: HVO local commanders assert HZ HB jurisdiction; the joint Bosniak-Croat front weakens at the seams. Pale staff assess the post-Graz posture as compatible with continued Drina-front pressure.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HZ HB lets Graz framework do its work

pending_event_notifications.body: HZ HB Presidency continues to frame Heliodrom, Dretelj, and Gabela as 'POW arrangements' and 'voluntary collection centers.' Sarajevo registers Zagreb patron pressure rising as international attention fixes on the Herzegovina detention sites.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO Presidency denies detention regime (ICTY Prlic IT-04-74-T)

pending_event_notifications.body: HZ HB Presidency contests ICRC framings of the Heliodrom and Dretelj sites. Pale notes the Zagreb patron-channel friction now mirroring the August 1992 Belgrade pattern.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO Presidency denies detention regime (ICTY Prlic IT-04-74-T)

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar orders Blaškić to consolidate the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle and the Žepče exclave. Sarajevo reads the airbridge sustainment as politically conditional but operationally durable; the central-Bosnia front hardens through 1993.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO digs in to hold central-Bosnia pocket

pending_event_notifications.body: Herceg-Bosna consolidates HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia defense through the Croatia airbridge. Pale reads the ARBiH-HVO war as locked into prolonged attrition; the partition map favors Pale's diplomatic position.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO sustains central-Bosnia defensive pockets

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB acknowledges the 51:49 map via the Federation channel. Sarajevo reads the move as Washington-track consolidation, with Croat constitutive-nation status preserved inside the Federation entity.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar accepts Contact Group framework

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar acts through the Federation channel established by the Washington Agreement. Pale sees the Federation track strengthened diplomatically; RS rejection becomes the isolated position.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HZ HB signs Contact Group framework

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar accepts the parallel-commands status quo. Sarajevo reads the move as HVO preserving the Zagreb-Susak channel and the Mostar Defence Department line; the Federation Army architecture holds nominally without forcing institutional merger on the Croat side.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO retains parallel command chain

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB allows the Federation Army architecture to remain on paper while HVO and ARBiH retain separate national chains. Pale assesses a Federation framework with persistent institutional friction on the Croat side; HVO military integration is nominal rather than substantive.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar accepts parallel Federation commands

pending_event_notifications.body: Herceg-Bosna signals federation language NOW (October-December 1993), pre-empting US pressure and shaping the eventual Washington framework architecture. Sarajevo reads the backchannel as Tudjman's strategic recalculation and the beginning of the Federation track three months ahead of formal signature.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar extends federation backchannel to Sarajevo

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar extends federation language to Sarajevo via the Galbraith and Swoboda channels. Pale reads the diplomatic recalibration: Tudjman is accommodating US pressure rather than resisting it, and the Croat-Bosniak war strain may ease ahead of the Washington Agreement framework.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HZ HB opens federation backchannel with Sarajevo

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB acknowledges the Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics framework. Sarajevo reads the move as Croat-Serb partition consolidation; the Federation track recedes while the central Bosnia war continues without a joint-front settlement.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar signs the Invincible package

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg framework as a constitutive ethnic republic. Pale sees the second signature on the partition map and weighs its own posture.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Boban signs Union of Three Republics

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar signals that Herceg-Bosna will organize as a Croat political entity with Zagreb's support. Sarajevo staff read the choice as a direct strain on the anti-VRS front.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Herceg-Bosna follows Zagreb line

pending_event_notifications.body: Croat leaders align their project with Zagreb and local territorial control. Pale analysts see the Bosniak-Croat alliance weakening even while HVO units still face VRS lines.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Herceg-Bosna sharpens Croat territorial claim

pending_event_notifications.body: The HZ HB Presidency keeps the Vance-Owen / Owen-Stoltenberg Banovina-aligned scope as the operative claim line. Sarajevo reads the cantons-plus framing as preserving the Federation-track availability when sanctions pressure on Croatia tightens at the Washington framework.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar holds cantons-plus scope at peak territorial reach

pending_event_notifications.body: The HZ HB Presidency stays inside the cantons-plus Banovina template under Tudjman scope-restraint pressure. Pale reads the diplomatic-track preservation against the partition logic the Graz 1992 joint statement signaled.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar declines open-conquest framing

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB acknowledges the Vance-Owen ten-province framework. Sarajevo reads the move as Zagreb-directed partition consolidation; three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) are ratified, and the central-Bosnia friction over the provincial allocation continues without a joint-front settlement.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar signs Vance-Owen at Athens

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB accepts the Vance-Owen framework. Pale sees the second signature on a partition map and weighs the Pale Assembly's pending response toward the same framework.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Boban signs Vance-Owen for HZ HB

pending_event_notifications.body: HZ HB accepts the formal Washington framework without reservation. Sarajevo reads the move as a clear Federation commitment, with joint anti-VRS coordination and Croatian supply access now politically easier to sustain.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar commits to the Federation

pending_event_notifications.body: HZ HB leadership commits fully to the formal Washington Agreement. Pale sees a consolidated Federation front, tighter Croat-Bosniak coordination, and reopened Croatian supply channels against the VRS.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mostar embraces the Federation

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar accepts open HV operational coordination. Sarajevo reads the September push as a Zagreb-led campaign that will shape the Dayton map; ARBiH 5th Corps coordinates on the Una-Sana axis.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HV and HVO under joint command in western Bosnia

pending_event_notifications.body: HV Guards Brigades are operating inside Bosnia under joint command with HVO. Pale assesses a multi-axis western-Bosnia offensive with Zagreb's full logistical backbone.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Croatian Army crosses border openly

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH acknowledges Western pressure to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. HVO staff see a more cooperative diplomatic posture, even as Sarajevo absorbs internal strain.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo engages Vance-Owen pressure

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH signals that it will engage with the Vance-Owen process to preserve international support. Pale sees Sarajevo trading some leverage for patron confidence.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo answers Western pressure

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo takes the Western warning seriously and tempers talk of aggressive offensives after the Federation framework. Mostar sees less risk of destabilizing the new arrangement, with some cost to RBiH leverage.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH accepts restraint message

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH acknowledges Western warnings against exploiting the post-Washington military window. Pale sees lower immediate offensive pressure, but also a Sarajevo leadership keeping patron confidence intact.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo heeds post-Washington restraint

pending_event_notifications.body: RS political leadership backs away from removing Mladic. Mostar sees the VRS officer corps hold together, while Pale's authority over the army looks visibly weakened.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Mladic survives Pale challenge

pending_event_notifications.body: Karadzic retreats from the dismissal attempt and Mladic remains in command. Sarajevo sees VRS command continuity restored, but the political-military split inside RS is now exposed.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale backs down before Mladic

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH subscribes to the Statement of Principles alongside the other Bosnian delegations. HVO staff read the move as improved international standing, with possible constraints on operations.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo subscribes to the London Principles

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH subscribes to a diplomatic line framed around ceasefire, ending ethnic cleansing, and lifting sieges. Pale reads the decision as a credibility gain for Sarajevo, but also as a constraint on RBiH military freedom.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo subscribes to the London Principles

pending_event_notifications.body: The Bosnian Assembly votes down the Union of Three Republics plan, refusing the Drina enclaves and Posavina corridor cession. HVO leaders see Sarajevo preserve its sovereignty claim and negotiating leverage while accepting the cost to international standing.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo Assembly rejects Owen-Stoltenberg

pending_event_notifications.body: The Bosnian Assembly votes down the Invincible package outright. Pale sees Sarajevo refuse partition on principle, prolonging the war and frustrating the ICFY mediators.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo Assembly rejects Owen-Stoltenberg

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg framework and gains international relief. HVO leaders see Sarajevo conceding the principle of a unified Bosnia under a tripartite republic formula.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the proposed union of ethnic republics, improving diplomatic credibility while conceding the unity principle. Pale sees Sarajevo moving onto the mediator track.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo's lift-and-strike diplomatic offensive lands on the US Senate agenda and the Contact Group track. Mostar reads the asymmetric-application argument with mixed receptivity: the lift narrative strengthens the Federation-track alignment but the strike narrative could escalate the broader war.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH presses Washington for lift-and-strike

pending_event_notifications.body: Izetbegović addresses the UN General Assembly and Silajdžić runs the Washington-London-Bonn shuttle demanding embargo lift and NATO air strikes. Pale reads the moral-high-ground appeal in Western opinion and prepares for sharpened US/EU diplomatic pressure ahead of the next Contact Group framework.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo escalates lift-and-strike diplomatic offensive

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo accepts the 51:49 framework under Christopher's pressure. Mostar reads the move as Washington-track consolidation, with Federation diplomacy aligned for the Contact Group signature.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH signs Contact Group framework

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the 51:49 map under US pressure with reservations on the eastern enclaves. Pale sees the Federation track strengthened diplomatically; RS rejection becomes the isolated position.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Contact Group framework

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo accepts the parallel-commands status quo. Mostar reads the move as Bosniak respect for HVO operational independence; the Federation Army architecture holds nominally without forcing institutional merger.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Federation Army stays on paper

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH allows the Federation Army architecture to remain on paper while ARBiH and HVO retain separate national chains. Pale assesses a Federation framework with persistent institutional friction; military integration is nominal rather than substantive.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts parallel Federation commands

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo greenlights the multi-corps push paired with HV-HVO Mistral 2. Mostar reads the September window as the Federation territorial-reintegration moment ahead of Dayton.
pending_event_notifications.headline: ARBiH commits to coordinated Federation offensives

pending_event_notifications.body: 5th Corps breaks out of Bihać; 3rd and 7th Corps press the central-Bosnia flank. Pale assesses a coordinated Federation offensive whose September weight will close the late-war territorial picture against RS.
pending_event_notifications.headline: ARBiH joins HV-HVO multi-front offensive

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo's command structure preserves multi-ethnic composition. Mostar reads the Federation-track signal: the civic platform that would underwrite a future Washington-track alignment with HRHB holds at the institutional level.
pending_event_notifications.headline: ARBiH keeps Croat officers and recruits

pending_event_notifications.body: ARBiH command at HQ Sarajevo declares retention of the Serb and Croat officer corps and the multi-ethnic recruitment pool. Pale reads the declaration as a civic-legitimacy reinforcement against partition claims; the Divjak-at-Sarajevo-HQ posture remains intact.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo affirms multi-ethnic ARBiH composition

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo's Presidency accepts the symmetric HWEZ regime and cooperates with UNPROFOR. Mostar reads the move as a Federation-aligned diplomatic posture that strengthens the Washington track.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH supports NATO Sarajevo ultimatum

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH cooperates with UNPROFOR collection-point inventories and publicly supports NATO enforcement. Pale faces a consolidated diplomatic posture in Sarajevo and the credible threat of air strikes if the VRS does not comply with the 21 February deadline.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts NATO HWEZ symmetric application

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo records refusal of the parallel paramilitary track; irregulars must integrate into ARBiH regiments or stand down. Mostar staff note the contrast with HVO practice and weigh the alliance implications.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH formalizes integration-only paramilitary line

pending_event_notifications.body: The Presidency formalizes refusal of irregular formations on the ARBiH order of battle. Pale reads the policy as a continuation of Sarajevo's integration line and a deliberate distance from the RS rear-area pattern.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo refuses parallel paramilitary track

pending_event_notifications.body: The Sarajevo Presidency records the maximalist civic-state claim as operative policy but keeps the pre-Washington HRHB federation channel open via U.S. shuttle diplomacy. Mostar reads the posture as compatible with the Croat-Bosniak rapprochement track Tudjman and Boban are working through.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo holds maximalist claim with HRHB channel open

pending_event_notifications.body: The Sarajevo Presidency records its operative policy: one Bosnia, equal citizenship, all pre-war territory legitimately RBiH. Reintegration proceeds principally through military pressure plus diplomatic legitimacy advocacy. No federation or autonomy offer is tabled toward RS-held communities. Pale reads the posture as institutional continuity with the May Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen and the September Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo maintains maximalist territorial claim

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo's civic line keeps a shared-state option alive on paper. Croat leaders weigh whether the pledge protects local autonomy or masks wartime centralization.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH platform stresses equal citizenship

pending_event_notifications.body: The Presidency publicly frames Bosnia as a multi-ethnic republic. Pale reads the statement as an effort to preserve international legitimacy and complicate partition claims.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo affirms civic republic platform

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the formal Washington framework without reservation. Mostar reads the move as a clear Federation commitment, with joint anti-VRS coordination and Croatian supply access now politically easier to sustain.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo embraces the Federation

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH Presidency commits fully to the Washington Agreement. Pale faces a consolidated Federation front, stronger international standing for Sarajevo, and reopened Croatian supply channels.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo signs the Federation framework

pending_event_notifications.body: Republika Srpska accepts the Pale assembly vote against Vance-Owen and continues the war. HVO leaders see RS internal cohesion preserved while Belgrade's anger and international isolation grow.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale accepts the assembly rejection

pending_event_notifications.body: Republika Srpska accepts the assembly's rejection of Vance-Owen. Sarajevo sees the comprehensive peace proposal fail while Pale preserves cohesion and absorbs heavier outside pressure.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS assembly rejection stands

pending_event_notifications.body: RS leaders reject the autonomy fallback envelope Belgrade has signalled through Patriarch Pavle and the Owen-Stoltenberg track. Mostar reads the platform-defence posture and the patron-channel friction; the maximalist territorial claim holds.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Karadzic rejects Belgrade autonomy framework

pending_event_notifications.body: RS leadership rejects the negotiated-autonomy fallback frameworks Belgrade has signalled. The Six Strategic Goals platform holds; the patron channel will absorb the friction; Pale signals that Republika Srpska is a state, not an autonomous province within BiH. Sarajevo reads the rejection of fallback envelopes as a hardening of the maximalist platform.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale crystallizes independence trajectory

pending_event_notifications.body: Pale defies Belgrade's soft diplomatic pressure on the corridor and Sarajevo axes. Mostar reads the FRY-RS friction as a leading indicator but no embargo; the patron channel holds at reduced confidence.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Karadzic rejects Milosevic's envoys

pending_event_notifications.body: RS rejects FRY pressure to ease the corridor tempo and align with the Owen-Stoltenberg envelope. Sarajevo reads the patron-channel friction but no material rupture — Pale's platform holds even as Belgrade's diplomatic envelope narrows.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale defies Belgrade on diplomatic envelope

pending_event_notifications.body: Pale refuses the Contact Group map and accepts the patron-rupture consequences. Mostar sees the Federation track strengthened diplomatically while the military pressure on RS hardens.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Assembly rejects 51/49 framework

pending_event_notifications.body: The Bosnian Serb Assembly records the documented Bijeljina position. Sarajevo reads the rejection as confirmation that the Federation track will continue without an RS settlement; Belgrade's embargo is now expected within weeks.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale rejects the Contact Group map

pending_event_notifications.body: RS accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg framework as a constitutive ethnic republic. Mostar sees the diplomatic legitimization of Republika Srpska advance and weighs its own posture.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Karadzic signs Union of Three Republics

pending_event_notifications.body: RS acknowledges the Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics framework as legitimization of Republika Srpska. Sarajevo reads the second signature on the partition map; the Drina-valley axis and Sarajevo division are preserved inside the tripartite frame.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale signs the Invincible package

pending_event_notifications.body: RS leaders confirm volunteer formations remain on local-request authority. Mostar staff note the policy hardens the rear-area pattern across the Krajina and Drina.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale formalizes paramilitary tolerance

pending_event_notifications.body: Pale records standing authorization for Arkan-style formations to operate alongside regular VRS units. Sarajevo reads the policy as a continuation of the rear-area pattern documented since Bijeljina.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Presidency authorizes paramilitary standing orders

pending_event_notifications.body: RS adoption of the Six Goals sharpens corridor and ethnic-separation claims that bear on western Herzegovina; Mostar leadership weighs patron consultation.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Karadzic Assembly clarifies territorial reach

pending_event_notifications.body: Belgrade-aligned deputies adopt Karadzic's territorial maximalist platform. Sarajevo intelligence reads this as a hardening of war aims; federal options narrow.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Assembly endorses Six Strategic Goals

pending_event_notifications.body: The Pale Assembly records non-engagement with the Federation framework. Mostar reads the move as the Six Goals platform staying intact; RS posture toward the joint anti-VRS Federation hardens.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS refuses Washington engagement

pending_event_notifications.body: Karadzic and Krajisnik decline to engage the Federation track. Sarajevo reads the non-engagement as confirmation that RS will treat the Washington framework as hostile diplomatic territory; the Federation track strengthens by default.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale ignores the Washington framework

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Mostar sees Sarajevo trying to satisfy UNPROFOR supervision without leaving the enclave fully exposed.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Pale sees formal compliance language paired with an effort to keep minimum defense capability inside the enclave.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament

pending_event_notifications.body: Mostar orders HVO leaders to secure current holdings and push for more. Sarajevo reads the posture as another strain on any remaining Bosniak-Croat coordination.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Herceg-Bosna presses Croat objectives

pending_event_notifications.body: Herceg-Bosna prioritizes Croat territorial objectives and accepts greater international pressure. Pale sees the Bosniak-Croat line weakening under competing aims.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HVO posture turns more assertive

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts mediation terms to rest and rearm. HVO staff note the logistical benefit for Sarajevo, even as internal critics frame the pause as weakness.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts a ceasefire pause

pending_event_notifications.body: Sarajevo chooses a temporary pause to recover supply and cohesion. Pale reads the lower aggression as useful, but not as a final settlement.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RBiH accepts ceasefire terms

pending_event_notifications.body: Pale orders VRS formations to fortify existing positions and rebuild supply. HVO planners expect fewer new thrusts, but stronger prepared defenses.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS shifts to holding current gains

pending_event_notifications.body: RS leadership favors digging in over costly advances. Sarajevo sees a defensive posture built around corridors, the Drina, and approaches to the capital.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Pale consolidates its holdings

pending_event_notifications.body: RS uses gradual releases to seek limits on further NATO action. Mostar sees a partial de-escalation that still leaves RS credibility badly damaged.
pending_event_notifications.headline: VRS starts phased hostage release

pending_event_notifications.body: RS begins releasing hostages in exchange for guarantees and concessions. Sarajevo sees some diplomatic damage contained, but NATO hesitation remains part of the exchange.
pending_event_notifications.headline: VRS trades UN hostage releases

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH follows Washington's demand to stop the advance and move toward negotiations. Mostar sees the military push capped for now, with the Federation's diplomatic position preserved.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts halt order

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the US demand to stop short of Banja Luka and pursue peace from its current gains. Pale sees immediate pressure ease, but the Federation keeps international credibility and a strong negotiating position.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Federation accepts Washington halt

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen Plan, improving international credibility while accepting a framework that legitimizes territorial losses. HVO leaders see Sarajevo moving into the same diplomatic channel.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen terms

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen framework and gains international credibility. Pale sees Sarajevo accepting the partition formula while pressure shifts toward the Bosnian Serb assembly.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB officials are touring HVO positions along the Sava line, signaling continued attention to the northern front.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HRHB Leadership Visits Posavina Positions

pending_event_notifications.body: HRHB officials are touring HVO positions along the Sava line, signaling continued attention to the northern front.
pending_event_notifications.headline: HRHB Leadership Visits Posavina Positions

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH brings foreign journalists into the visit and emphasizes the human cost of the siege. Mostar sees stronger international messaging, but less pure command presence.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo turns front visit into press event

pending_event_notifications.body: RBiH converts the visit into an international media event about siege conditions. Pale sees Sarajevo trading command focus for diplomatic pressure.
pending_event_notifications.headline: Sarajevo brings foreign press to front visit

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency is emphasizing the Posavina corridor and the forces holding the northern link between RS territories.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Leadership Visits Posavina Corridor

pending_event_notifications.body: The RS presidency is emphasizing the Posavina corridor and the forces holding the northern link between RS territories.
pending_event_notifications.headline: RS Leadership Visits Posavina Corridor
